title: A Simple Linear Flowchart
objectives: Turn simple, non-branching pseudocode into a flowchart

hook.text: Turning pseudocode into a flowchart is like telling the same story in a different language: the content stays the same, only the presentation changes.

concept.heading: Linear (non-branching) flowchart
concept.body: The simplest kind of flowchart has no decisions at all and follows a single path: Start → Input → Process → Output → End. Each line of pseudocode matches exactly one symbol.

concept.heading: From pseudocode to flowchart
concept.body: "READ a" becomes an input/output symbol, "total ← a + b" becomes a process symbol, and "WRITE total" becomes an input/output symbol again. Each line, in order from top to bottom, matches one symbol and one arrow.

exercises.question: Build the flowchart for the algorithm "add two numbers and print the result".
How many different exit paths can a linear flowchart have?
options: As many as the number of decisions

feedback.correct: Correct. A linear flowchart has no branching, so there is only one path.
feedback.incorrect: A linear (non-branching) flowchart has no decision symbol, so only a single path is followed.

exercises.question: Put the steps of the algorithm that calculates the area of a rectangle in the correct order.
How many "Start" terminals should a flowchart have?

feedback.correct: Correct. Every algorithm has exactly one starting point.
feedback.incorrect: An algorithm must have a clear start: exactly one "Start" terminal.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: In a flowchart, every chart begins with exactly one ___ symbol.

summary: A linear flowchart has no decisions (branching) and follows a single path.
Each line of pseudocode matches a symbol, and each move from one line to the next matches an arrow.
A flowchart always begins with a Start terminal and ends with an End terminal.
